original_test_intent: Verify that BIOS Package C-State limits C0/C1, C2 and C6 produce the source-defined PC2/PC6 package residency behavior after each save/reset and OS boot.
original_method: A qualified operator records the current BIOS setting, applies one approved limit at a time and reboots; after stable boot, collect full PTAT/cpupower/turbostat evidence across all CPU packages under a defined idle/workload window, normalize PC2/PC6 units and compare the complete three-state matrix; finally restore the approved setting and verify boot health.
manual_activity: The owner approves supported options, tools, observation conditions, maintenance/recovery and final setting; an operator performs each BIOS save/reset and confirms boot; the owner decides the verdict.

Approved Package C-State recipe and exact supported option labels
PTAT/cpupower/turbostat versions, output-field mapping and PC2/PC6 semantics
Idle/workload preparation, observation duration, sample cadence and nonzero tolerance
Console/BIOS access, maintenance window and failed-boot recovery path
Current and approved final BIOS settings plus secure OS access
safety_requirements: Keep BIOS writes and save/reset under qualified operator control and explicit approval
Record before/after settings and restore the approved final configuration
Do not use plaintext credentials or disable host-key verification
Do not sample only cpu0, one instant or tail-truncated output
Do not write OS cpuidle or CPU power policy as part of evidence collection
Stop on failed boot, unsupported option, missing counters, topology change or thermal/power anomaly
No automatic BIOS toggling or retry

Prepare per-option commands and collect full OS residency after operator-confirmed boots
Normalize PC2/PC6 per CPU package and compare the exact source matrix

Perform no BIOS write/save/reset, credential bypass, recovery decision or DUT verdict

Approve maintenance, operator sequence, recovery and final restored setting
Review all three per-option datasets and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.command_recommendation: After each operator-confirmed BIOS boot, use securely authenticated full PTAT/cpupower/turbostat collection for every CPU package over the approved observation window; retain untruncated output and exits.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2043 Wistron-BIOS-00492-V002: approve exact supported Package C-State option labels, PTAT/cpupower/turbostat versions and PC2/PC6 field mapping, all-package aggregation, idle/workload duration and zero/nonzero tolerance; define maintenance, failed-boot recovery and final restored BIOS setting while preserving the C0/C1, C2 and C6 criteria matrix.

review_improvement: Converts PARTIAL into an approved hybrid class, restores the complete option matrix, removes insecure/truncated shortcuts and makes BIOS recovery and final restoration explicit.
independent_technical_reasoning: Package C-state residency is distinct from core cpuidle state availability, so inspecting cpu0 state names cannot prove PC2/PC6 behavior. Residency is a percentage or time accumulation over an interval and can remain zero under load even when a state is allowed. Each BIOS limit therefore needs an identical observation protocol across every package, and state-changing BIOS transitions require operator control and recovery planning.
